Purpose and scope

This policy sets out how Alderbridge Care Group manages and staff use company vehicles, including the
minibus used for resident outings and pool cars used for community visits. It applies to any staff member
authorised to drive an Alderbridge vehicle.

Policy statement

A company vehicle is driven safely, legally and courteously by an authorised, appropriately licensed driver,
and maintained to a standard that keeps residents, staff and the public safe.

Definitions

**Authorised driver** a staff member whose licence has been checked and who is listed on the site's
approved driver list. **Pool car** a vehicle shared between staff for community visits, booked in advance.
**Daily walkaround check** the brief visual and functional check completed before a vehicle's first use
each day.

Roles and responsibilities

**The registered manager** maintains the approved driver list and checks each driver's licence annually.
**The driver** completes the daily walkaround check before first use and reports any defect immediately.
**Facilities** arranges servicing, MOT and any repair a walkaround check identifies.

Purpose and scope

This guidance explains how manual handling equipment, including a hoist and sling, is used safely at Alderbridge Care Group. It applies to every member of care staff performing a resident transfer.

Policy statement

A hoist or sling is checked before use, with a weight-limit cross-check, operated by at least two staff members holding an equipment-type-specific competency sign-off, now required for every distinct equipment model in use, with a defective item quarantined and tagged rather than simply set aside.

Definitions

**Pre-use check** the check completed before every use. **Weight-limit cross-check** the check against the resident's current recorded weight. **Equipment-type-specific sign-off** the new requirement, introduced in this version, confirming competency on each distinct hoist or sling model in use, not only general manual handling training. **Quarantine and tagging** the new process, introduced in this version, physically marking and isolating a defective item from further use until repaired or disposed of.

Roles and responsibilities

**Care staff** complete the pre-use check and weight-limit cross-check, and now hold a specific competency sign-off for each distinct equipment model they use. **Facilities** arranges 6-monthly LOLER inspection and now manages the quarantine and tagging process for a defective item. **The registered manager** ensures a staff member's equipment-specific sign-off is current for every model available at their site.

1. Complete a pre-use check of the hoist and sling before every use.

Lone Working Policy

Purpose and scope

This policy sets out how Alderbridge Care Group protects staff who work without a colleague physically present, most significantly the community support workers at Willow Bank Community Service who visit people supported in their own homes. It applies to every member of staff whose role involves any period of genuinely unaccompanied work, whether that is a community visit, an early or late shift where they are briefly the only person on site, or an out-of-hours facilities check.

Policy statement

Alderbridge does not treat lone working as an unavoidable, unmanageable feature of community-based care; it is planned for, monitored, and supported with technology and clear escalation routes specifically because the risk profile of working alone, in an unfamiliar or unpredictable environment, is genuinely different from working within a staffed building.

Definitions

**Lone worker** anyone carrying out an activity alone, without close or direct supervision, for a defined period. **Check-in** the confirmation, via the mobile lone-worker app, that a lone worker has arrived at or completed a scheduled activity safely. **Welfare call** the call made to a lone worker who has missed a scheduled check-in, to confirm their safety. **Escalation** the process followed where a welfare call goes unanswered, involving a supervisor attending the location.

Roles and responsibilities

**Every community support worker** checks in at the start and end of every visit using the mobile lone-worker app, and withdraws from any situation that feels unsafe rather than persisting to complete a task. **The Willow Bank office** monitors check-ins in real time and initiates a welfare call the moment a check-in is overdue. **A duty supervisor** attends the address in person if a welfare call goes unanswered, and escalates to the police immediately if there is any indication of a genuine emergency.

Confirm every booking in writing by email before the shift; the previous allowance for verbal telephone confirmation in an urgent case has been removed, since a written record now exists for every booking regardless of urgency.

Confirm the agency worker's DBS check and mandatory training status with the agency before the shift is confirmed, not after they arrive.

Deliver the shortened site induction on arrival, covering fire safety, safeguarding contacts and medication boundaries specific to that site.

Agency staff must never administer controlled drugs, even if qualified to do so at their home organisation, unless they have separately completed Alderbridge's own controlled drugs competency check.

Supervise a new agency worker's first shift more closely than an established one, checking in with them and observing their practice.

Record any concern about an agency worker's conduct or competence and feed it back to the agency, escalating to the registered manager if serious.

Exceptions and professional judgement

Where a genuinely urgent, unforeseen gap arises outside the approved agencies' normal availability (for example, overnight during a public holiday), the registered manager may contact a wider agency pool only with the Alderbridge Quality Lead's direct approval, and the same written-confirmation, DBS and training verification standard still applies in full regardless of the urgency — the removal of verbal confirmation applies without exception, including in this scenario.

Local and regional variations

The two approved framework agencies are chosen for their coverage of each region; Willow Bank's community model means agency use there is comparatively rare and reserved mainly for office cover rather than community visiting, which relies primarily on permanent staff given the trust and local knowledge community visiting depends on.

The check-in system, the welfare-call timings and the escalation process this policy sets out exist for one purpose: so that a community support worker is never genuinely alone in the sense that matters, even while physically alone in someone's home, because a structured, reliable safety net is always operating in the background whether or not it is ever actually needed on a given visit.

Lone Working Policy

Purpose and scope

This policy sets out how Alderbridge Care Group protects staff who work without a colleague physically present, most significantly the community support workers at Willow Bank Community Service who visit people supported in their own homes. It applies to every member of staff whose role involves any period of genuinely unaccompanied work, whether that is a community visit, an early or late shift where they are briefly the only person on site, or an out-of-hours facilities check.

Policy statement

Alderbridge does not treat lone working as an unavoidable, unmanageable feature of community-based care; it is planned for, monitored, and supported with technology and clear escalation routes specifically because the risk profile of working alone, in an unfamiliar or unpredictable environment, is genuinely different from working within a staffed building.

Definitions

**Lone worker** anyone carrying out an activity alone, without close or direct supervision, for a defined period. **Check-in** the confirmation, via the mobile lone-worker app, that a lone worker has arrived at or completed a scheduled activity safely. **Welfare call** the call made to a lone worker who has missed a scheduled check-in, to confirm their safety. **Escalation** the process followed where a welfare call goes unanswered, involving a supervisor attending the location.

Roles and responsibilities

**Every community support worker** checks in at the start and end of every visit using the mobile lone-worker app, and withdraws from any situation that feels unsafe rather than persisting to complete a task. **The Willow Bank office** monitors check-ins in real time and initiates a welfare call the moment a check-in is overdue. **A duty supervisor** attends the address in person if a welfare call goes unanswered, and escalates to the police immediately if there is any indication of a genuine emergency.

Lone Working Policy

Purpose and scope

This policy sets out how Alderbridge Care Group protects staff who work without a colleague physically present, most significantly the community support workers at Willow Bank Community Service who visit people supported in their own homes. It applies to every member of staff whose role involves any period of genuinely unaccompanied work, whether that is a community visit, an early or late shift where they are briefly the only person on site, or an out-of-hours facilities check.

Policy statement

Alderbridge does not treat lone working as an unavoidable, unmanageable feature of community-based care; it is planned for, monitored, and supported with technology and clear escalation routes specifically because the risk profile of working alone, in an unfamiliar or unpredictable environment, is genuinely different from working within a staffed building.

Definitions

**Lone worker** anyone carrying out an activity alone, without close or direct supervision, for a defined period. **Check-in** the confirmation, via the mobile lone-worker app, that a lone worker has arrived at or completed a scheduled activity safely. **Welfare call** the call made to a lone worker who has missed a scheduled check-in, to confirm their safety. **Escalation** the process followed where a welfare call goes unanswered, involving a supervisor attending the location.

Roles and responsibilities

**Every community support worker** checks in at the start and end of every visit using the mobile lone-worker app, and withdraws from any situation that feels unsafe rather than persisting to complete a task. **The Willow Bank office** monitors check-ins in real time and initiates a welfare call the moment a check-in is overdue. **A duty supervisor** attends the address in person if a welfare call goes unanswered, and escalates to the police immediately if there is any indication of a genuine emergency.

Purpose and scope

This policy sets out how Alderbridge Care Group protects staff who work without a colleague physically present, most significantly the community support workers at Willow Bank Community Service who visit people supported in their own homes. It applies to every member of staff whose role involves any period of genuinely unaccompanied work, whether that is a community visit, an early or late shift where they are briefly the only person on site, or an out-of-hours facilities check.

Policy statement

Alderbridge does not treat lone working as an unavoidable, unmanageable feature of community-based care; it is planned for, monitored, and supported with technology and clear escalation routes specifically because the risk profile of working alone, in an unfamiliar or unpredictable environment, is genuinely different from working within a staffed building.

Definitions

Roles and responsibilities

Lone Working Policy

Purpose and scope

This policy sets out how Alderbridge Care Group protects staff who work without a colleague physically present, most significantly the community support workers at Willow Bank Community Service who visit people supported in their own homes. It applies to every member of staff whose role involves any period of genuinely unaccompanied work, whether that is a community visit, an early or late shift where they are briefly the only person on site, or an out-of-hours facilities check.

Policy statement

Alderbridge does not treat lone working as an unavoidable, unmanageable feature of community-based care; it is planned for, monitored, and supported with technology and clear escalation routes specifically because the risk profile of working alone, in an unfamiliar or unpredictable environment, is genuinely different from working within a staffed building.

Definitions

**Lone worker** anyone carrying out an activity alone, without close or direct supervision, for a defined period. **Check-in** the confirmation, via the mobile lone-worker app, that a lone worker has arrived at or completed a scheduled activity safely. **Welfare call** the call made to a lone worker who has missed a scheduled check-in, to confirm their safety. **Escalation** the process followed where a welfare call goes unanswered, involving a supervisor attending the location.

Roles and responsibilities

**Every community support worker** checks in at the start and end of every visit using the mobile lone-worker app, and withdraws from any situation that feels unsafe rather than persisting to complete a task. **The Willow Bank office** monitors check-ins in real time and initiates a welfare call the moment a check-in is overdue. **A duty supervisor** attends the address in person if a welfare call goes unanswered, and escalates to the police immediately if there is any indication of a genuine emergency.
